stories.headline: NVIDIA SMASHES Q3 ESTIMATES WITH REVENUE UP 103%, LIFTS BUYBACK TO $227 BILLION AS BOARD CONFIRMS KRESS OVER HUANG
stories.body: Nvidia reported fiscal Q3 revenue of roughly $115.8 billion, up 103% year over year and above the ~$109 billion consensus, with adjusted EPS of $2.68 versus ~$2.47 expected and data-center revenue of about $107.6 billion; shares rose as much as 3-4% in after-hours trading even as the board confirmed interim CEO Colette Kress will continue running the company rather than reinstating Jensen Huang.
stories.explain: A beat-and-raise quarter moves a stock in after-hours trading because dealers and algorithmic market makers reprice the shares against consensus estimates that were already baked into the pre-earnings price, so what matters is the surprise versus expectations, not the absolute growth rate. Nvidia's Q4 revenue guidance of roughly $130 billion against a ~$125 billion Street estimate carries more weight than the trailing quarter because a stock's price reflects discounted future cash flows, which is also why the drop in guided gross margin to 71-72% from near 75% this quarter — a sign memory costs are rising faster than expected — is being read alongside the headline beat rather than ignored.

stories.headline: S&P 500 SINKS TO FIVE-MONTH LOW, DOW SHEDS 849 POINTS AS MEDICARE AUDIT FEARS AND PRE-EARNINGS CAUTION HIT ALL 11 SECTORS
stories.body: The S&P 500 closed down 1.07% at 7,341 — its lowest close in roughly five months — while the Nasdaq 100 fell 0.75% to 27,002 and the Dow dropped about 1.64% (849 points); health insurers led the slide after a proposed expansion of Medicare Advantage audits, and declining stocks outnumbered advancers by more than five to one.
stories.explain: A decline where all 11 S&P sectors finish lower and losers swamp winners five-to-one is a breadth signal that the selloff is macro-driven rather than concentrated in one story, which is a meaningfully different read for a portfolio manager than a single mega-cap dragging the index down on its own. Today's weakness front-ran Nvidia's earnings print specifically because options markets were pricing a large implied move into the stock, and uncertainty ahead of a high-weight constituent's report tends to suppress the whole tape until the print removes the overhang.

stories.headline: JPMORGAN PULLS FORWARD DECEMBER HIKE CALL AS TRADERS AWAIT OCT. PCE NOV. 25 AND NOVEMBER JOBS REPORT DEC. 4
stories.body: JPMorgan moved up its forecast to call for a quarter-point hike at the Dec. 8-9 FOMC meeting, adding to futures-implied odds that have hovered near 70-85% since Chair Kevin Warsh's Fed held rates at 3.75%-4% in October on a 10-2 vote with governors Cook and Hammack dissenting in favor of an immediate hike.
stories.explain: A bank 'pulling forward' a rate call means its economists now expect the move a meeting earlier than previously modeled, which matters because sell-side rate calls feed directly into the swaps and futures curves that price forward borrowing costs for mortgages, corporate debt, and leveraged loans well before the Fed actually acts. With both the October core PCE reading on Nov. 25 and the November jobs report on Dec. 4 landing in the eight days before the FOMC decision, those two releases are now the swing factor between a quarter-point hike and another hold, which is why futures-implied odds are still moving despite no new Fed commentary this week.

stories.headline: ANTHROPIC SETS IPO AT $70-$78 A SHARE, VALUING AI STARTUP UP TO $1.4 TRILLION — DOWN FROM $2 TRILLION TALK — AHEAD OF NOV. 19 NASDAQ DEBUT
stories.body: Anthropic's amended filing sets terms for 825 million Class A shares at $70 to $78 apiece, a raise of up to roughly $64.35 billion and a fully diluted valuation of up to about $1.4 trillion — well below the $2 trillion figure that circulated earlier this year — with trading expected to begin Nov. 19 on Nasdaq under ticker ANT; AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and TSMC have separately agreed to buy $26 billion of shares in a concurrent private placement.
stories.explain: The gap between the $2 trillion figure once floated and the $1.2-1.4 trillion range now in the filing is bookbuilding doing its job: underwriters test a price with the anchor investors who actually have to commit capital, and when their orders don't support the higher number, the range gets marked down before the deal ever opens to the public rather than risk a weak first trading day. That the same strategic buyers supplying $26 billion in the private placement are chipmakers and cloud providers whose own revenue depends on AI capex is also notable — it ties Anthropic's IPO pricing to the same demand picture Nvidia's earnings just tested.

stories.headline: HUANG REPORTEDLY AGREES TO TESTIFY AS HOUSE BRIEFING OVER ALLEGED CHINA SPY CONTACT PROCEEDS NOV. 18, DAY AFTER NVIDIA EARNINGS
stories.body: Despite stepping down as Nvidia's chairman and CEO, Jensen Huang has reportedly agreed to appear before the closed-door briefing three House committee chairs requested for Nov. 18 over his contacts with a Megaspeed executive U.S. intelligence agencies have flagged; neither Huang, Megaspeed, nor the executive has been charged, and Nvidia maintains the meetings were ordinary customer business.
stories.explain: A voluntary closed-door briefing — as opposed to a subpoenaed hearing — lets lawmakers gather information without the procedural threshold of proving wrongdoing first, which is why it can proceed even though the underlying espionage claims remain unproven and Huang has already left the company. The timing compounds the overhang for Nvidia's new leadership: a briefing landing one day after Colette Kress's first earnings call as CEO means any disclosure about export-control or trade-secret risk would land squarely in the news cycle still digesting the Q3 print and the Anthropic IPO's AI-demand read-through.

watchlist: October core PCE inflation data — Nov. 25, the last major print before the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting
November jobs report — Dec. 4, landing four days before the FOMC decision
Fed's Dec. 8-9 FOMC meeting — hike odds near 70-85% after JPMorgan pulled its call forward to December
Anthropic's Nasdaq debut under ticker ANT — expected Nov. 19 after pricing at $70-$78/share, up to a $1.4 trillion valuation
Jensen Huang's closed-door House briefing on alleged China spy contact — Nov. 18, his first major appearance since leaving Nvidia's board confirmed it would not reinstate him

deepDive.title: Why Nvidia's Stock Can Rally After Hours on a Day the Market Fell
content: Today's session and today's earnings print told two different stories. The S&P 500 closed at a five-month low, with all 11 sectors down and decliners outnumbering advancers more than five to one, partly on caution ahead of Nvidia's report. Then, after the bell, Nvidia posted revenue up 103% year over year and guided next quarter above Wall Street's estimate, and the stock jumped in after-hours trading — even as the board confirmed it would not reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. Understanding why a single earnings print can override both a down macro tape and a leadership crisis in the same day comes down to how extended-hours price discovery actually works.

A stock's price is the market's estimate of the present value of its future cash flows, and by the time a widely covered company like Nvidia reports, analyst consensus — the ~$109 billion revenue estimate and ~$125 billion Q4 guide the Street expected — is already embedded in the pre-print price. What moves the stock is the surprise relative to that embedded expectation, not the absolute growth rate: a 103% year-over-year revenue increase that merely matched consensus would barely move the tape, while beating it by roughly $7 billion and guiding next quarter nearly $5 billion above estimates forces institutional desks and market makers to reprice in thin after-hours liquidity, which is also why the percentage move AH often overshoots or reverses once full-day volume resumes.

What gets missed is that guidance usually outweighs the trailing quarter because price is forward-looking almost by construction — the quarter that just closed is already sunk, but the guide is the market's best update on the next one. The clearest historical parallel is Meta's February 2022 report: decent quarterly results but a light forward guide sent shares down 26% in a single session, wiping out roughly $230 billion in market value, because the miss was in expectations for the future, not the past. Nvidia's compressing gross-margin guidance — down to 71-72% from near 75% this quarter on rising memory costs — is the same forward-looking signal working in the other direction, a flag analysts will model into the stock's multiple even on an otherwise blowout print.

That read-through matters beyond Nvidia itself right now. A guide this strong argues that AI-related capital spending is still accelerating heading into year-end, which is exactly the kind of resilient-demand signal the Fed will weigh against October's core PCE data on Nov. 25 and the jobs report on Dec. 4 before its Dec. 8-9 meeting — strength here leans toward the hawkish case JPMorgan just pulled forward. It also lands squarely on top of Anthropic's IPO bookbuilding, due to price before Nasdaq trading begins Nov. 19: investors sizing up how much to pay for Anthropic's projected AI cash flows now have a fresh, concrete data point for how much real demand exists upstream in the same ecosystem.
